rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A tradition says Joseph and the king met Jacob's household with four thousand troops and state officials, accompanied by Egypt's people.
rows.anchor: Rivayet olunur ki Yûsuf ve Melik maiyyetlerinde dört bin asker ve ricâl-i devlet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob, leaning on Judah, asks whether the approaching Egyptian ruler is Pharaoh; Judah answers that he is Jacob's son.
rows.anchor: “ey Yehuda, şu Mısır’ın firavunu mu?” diye sordu, “hayır, oğlun” dedi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob greets Joseph first, calling him the one who removes sorrows.
rows.anchor: Yûsuf’tan evvel Ya‘kūb selâm verdi de “selâm sana ey hüzünleri gideren” dedi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph welcomes his parents by embracing them and settling them in a private place to rest.
rows.anchor: ebeveynini kendine îvâ etti yani boyunlarına sarılıp bağrına basarak menzil-i mahsûsunda istirahat ettirdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The embrace and lodging occur at the reception site before the family enters the city.
rows.anchor: anlaşılıyor ki bu henüz şehre girmeden istikbal mevki‘inde oluyordu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph then invites the whole family to enter Egypt safely, by God's will.
rows.anchor: ve “inşallah hepiniz emn ü eman içinde Mısır’a giriniz” dedi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph gives his parents exceptional honor, raising them onto the elevated palace structure that served as a throne.
rows.anchor: kendisinin bir taht gibi olan yüksek köşkünün üzerine çıkardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The family prostrates as an act of gratitude to God for Joseph; Elmalılı ultimately finds this reading the better fit.
rows.anchor: Yûsuf için Allah’a şükür olmak üzere secdeye kapandılar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the prostration as the customary bodily greeting offered to Joseph in that era.
rows.anchor: Bir kavle göre ise, o zaman âdet olduğu üzere Yûsuf’a karşı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers gratitude because a greeting prostration would more naturally have occurred at the first meeting.
rows.anchor: lâkin selam secdesi olsa idi ilk mülâkatta yapılması daha zâhir olurdu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dream's wording can mean either that the family prostrated to Joseph or prostrated for him, allowing both senses.
rows.anchor: “bana secde ediyorlar gördüm” demek olabileceği gibi, “benim için secde ediyorlar gördüm” de demek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prostration also recalls the resemblance between this scene and the angels' prostration before Adam.
rows.anchor: meleklerin Âdem’e secdesi mânası beynindeki münasebet ve müşâbehet unutulmamak lâzım gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph calls the present scene the actual realization of the dream, beyond Jacob's earlier concise, interpretive explanation.
rows.anchor: o zaman senin yaptığın tevil ilmî ve icmâlî bir tâbir idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made Joseph's earlier dream come true as a faithful, literal event.
rows.anchor: onu Rabbim hakikaten hak kıldı sâdık ve tıpkı gördüğüm gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Vahidi and others give bedv two senses: an open flat place where someone appears from afar, and a place named Bada.
rows.anchor: Vâhidî vesâirenin beyânına göre “bedv” iki mânaya gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In its first sense, bedv derives from bada, appearing, and names open country, contrasted with settled hadar; the related forms are bedewi and hadari.
rows.anchor: بدا يبدو fiilinden zuhûr mânasına masdar olup sonra mekân, masdar ile tesmiye edilerek “bedv” ve mukabilinde “hadar”

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Jacob moved to and lived in a place called Bada, where he had a mosque at the mountain's foot.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan rivayet [2927] olunduğuna göre Ya‘kūb “Bedâ” nâm mahalle

rows.speaker: İbn Enbârî
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari identifies Bada as a known location and cites the saying that someone is between Shu'b and Bada.
rows.anchor: İbn Enbârî de demiştir ki: “Bedâ” mâruf bir mevzi‘dir. هو بين شعب وبدا

rows.speaker: Küseyyir
rows.claim: Kuthayyir's verse names Shu'b and Bada as places familiar from poetry.
rows.anchor: Küseyyir şöyle demiştir: وَأَنْتِ الَّتِي حَبَّبْتِ شِعْبًا إِلَى بَدَا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb badā al-qawm means that a people arrived at Bada; on this reading Jacob's family were settled folk, not originally Bedouin, as 12:109 later supports.
rows.anchor: Ve bu suretle Hazret-i Ya‘kūb ve evlâdı esasen bedevî değil hadarî idiler demek olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even with the open-country sense, Joseph can mean that he brought the family from the countryside into Egypt.
rows.anchor: Sizi bâdiyeden geçirerek taşradan Mısır’a getirdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph counts his family's arrival and prosperity as a personal divine favor equal to his release from prison, and omits the well episode to spare his brothers.
rows.anchor: hânedânının nimet ve refâhını kendine ait bir ihsan saymış ve kardeşlerini müteessir etmemek için zindandan evvel olan kuyu vak‘asını tasrihten ictinab

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph treats the brothers' conflict as Satan's prompting to corrupt their relationship, not as an intrinsic fault to dwell on in either party.
rows.anchor: aramızı bozmak [2928] için Şeytan’ın bizlemesinden, ifsad ve iğvâsından ibaret idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The satanic instigation was a serious trial; God's favor prevented the evils that otherwise might have followed.
rows.anchor: Eğer Allah’ın ihsânı yetişmese idi ne fenalıklar olmazdı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's subtle planning for what He wills is delicate and gracious, and He alone possesses knowledge and wisdom.
rows.anchor: Dilediği emr için tedbîri ne latîf, ne hoş, ne incedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An anecdote says Jacob toured Joseph's treasuries and reproached him for not sending a letter across the eight-stage distance; Joseph says Gabriel had forbidden it.
rows.anchor: hazineleri gezdirmiş; altın, gümüş, cevâhir, elbise, silah vesâire hazinelerini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the same anecdote, Gabriel says God's order followed Jacob's earlier fear that a wolf might eat Joseph.
rows.anchor: korkarım ki kurt yer’ dediğinden dolayı Allah bana öyle emretti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further report says Jacob lived with Joseph for twenty-four years, died, and was buried by Joseph beside Isaac in Syria as he had requested; Joseph then lived twenty-three years more in Egypt.
rows.anchor: Ya‘kūb aleyhisselâm Yûsuf ile beraber yirmi dört sene yaşamış, sonra vefat etmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph understands worldly events as a dream whose outcome is realized through interpretation; his knowledge of their interpretation teaches him that an afterlife lies ahead.
rows.anchor: bütün dünya hâdisâtı tevil ve tâbiri sonunda tahakkuk edecek bir rüya gibidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is Joseph's master, patron, and benefactor in both worlds, so he asks to die in submission to Him.
rows.anchor: dünyada ve âhirette Sensin benim velîm mâlik-i emrim, veliyy-i nimetim, efendim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph asks to be joined after death with the righteous, like his forefathers, since that completes the blessing.
rows.anchor: ve sâlihîne ilhak eyle âhirette atalarım gibi sâlihler zümresinde haşreyle. Zira nimet ancak bununla tamam olacaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says God took Joseph's soul pure; Egyptians disputed his burial place, then placed him in a marble coffin in the Nile so all could share its blessing.
rows.anchor: Mısır ahâlisi beyninde defni husûsunda münâza‘a ve muhâsame zuhur etmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same report says Egypt's government passed from the Amalekites to the Pharaohs, who ruled the Israelites until Moses was commissioned.
rows.anchor: hükûmet Amâlika’dan çıkıp firavunlara intikal etmişti ve Benî İsrâil Hazret-i Mûsâ’nın bi‘setine kadar firavunların elinde kalmış idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The famous Ascension hadith says Muhammad met Adam in the lowest heaven and Joseph in the second.
rows.anchor: Mi‘râc gecesi Âdem’e semâ-i dünyada, Yûsuf’a ikinci semâda mülâkī olduğunu meşhur Mi‘râc hadisinde haber vermişti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph does not seek more Egyptian kingship despite his power: he sees worldly rule as a trial that ends, and longs instead for eternal life and a good end.
rows.anchor: daha ilerisine gitmek ve kuvvet elinde iken Mısır’a büsbütün melik

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Joseph account is an unseen report revealed to Muhammad, who was absent when Joseph's brothers plotted and when Quraysh and Jews met to devise their challenge.
rows.anchor: ne Yûsuf’u kuyuya atmak dolabını kuran kardeşlerin yanında idin ne de sana bir mekr olarak bunu sormak için gıyâbında konuşup karar veren Kureyş ile Yehûdun meclislerinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the revelation reports what only an eyewitness could know, and God is witness over all things, it confirms Muhammad as a true prophet.
rows.anchor: bu gayb haberlerinin عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ شَهِيدٌ [el-Mâide 5/117] olan Hak teâlâ’dan sana vahyedildiği

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people will not believe even if Muhammad ardently desires it; many dismiss revelation and the Joseph account as a novel or invented tale.
rows.anchor: Çokları vahye ve bu güzel kıssanın mündericâtına iman etmez; güzel bir roman, uydurma bir hikâye gibi tahayyül eder geçer

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad asks no payment for the revelation, removing grounds for suspicion; the Qur'an is a sincere reminder for rational beings throughout the worlds.
rows.anchor: bu ancak âlemîne bir zikirdir. Bu ihbar veya bu Kur’an bütün zevi’l-ukūl âlemlerine hakkı hatırlatmak için hâlis bir tezkir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sound-minded people should heed the warning, but those ruled by desire have lost the capacity to remember; hence most do not respond to reminders.
rows.anchor: akılları hevâlarına mağlup olmuş, tezekkür kābiliyetini zâyi‘eylemiş olanlar da ihtar ve tezkîre ehemmiyet vermeyip

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heavenly, earthly, inward, and outward signs attest God's existence, unity, knowledge, power, and wisdom, yet people pass them by through observation, experience, science, and philosophy while pursuing other aims.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın varlığına ve birliğine ve ilm ü kudretine ve kemâl-i hikmetine delâlet eden enfüsî, âfâkī, arzî, semâvî bunca delâil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people affirm God only while mixing belief with overt or hidden shirk, assigning worship to others besides Him; they lack pure monotheism.
rows.anchor: Allah’tan başkasına da mâbudluk pâyesi verir, mâsivâya da taparlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who ignore the signs and fail to prepare for the afterlife have no assurance against an encompassing punishment or the sudden Hour; their conduct reflects blindness, not safety.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın azâbından bürüme: yani hepsine şümûllü bir ukūbet gelivermesinden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad's way is to call people to God with insight, along the path of pure monotheism and sincere faith, and to declare God transcendent and free of shirk.
rows.anchor: işte bu bu davet, böyle tevhid ve ihlâs ile iman yolu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling to religion is proper only with understanding, sincerity, certainty, purity, wisdom, and devotion solely to God, rather than blind passion or ulterior motives.
rows.anchor: basiret üzere: ne dediğini bilerek, ihlâs ve yakīn üzere yürüyerek, nezâhet ve hikmet dairesinde ve ancak Allah için Allah’a davet edilmelidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command in 16:125 further explains the proper manner of inviting people to God's path.
rows.anchor: ٱدْعُ إِلَىٰ سَبِيلِ رَبِّكَ بِٱلْحِكْمَةِ وَٱلْمَوْعِظَةِ ٱلْحَسَنَةِ وَجَٰدِلْهُم بِٱلَّتِى هِىَ أَحْسَنُ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier messengers were men from settled towns whom God inspired, like Muhammad; they were neither angels, women, nor Bedouins.
rows.anchor: ne melâike, ne kadın, ne bedevî ne de başka bir şey değil, medenî insanlardan kendilerine vahiy

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's family, Abraham, and Isaac were originally settled people; Jacob's sojourn in the countryside was temporary, a passage, a mission to guide nomads, or a trial, as Moses also experienced.
rows.anchor: Bütün peygamberler ve İbrâhim ve İshak gibi Ya‘kūb da esasen ehl-i kurâdan, yani medenî idiler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even Adam was created with his spouse in Paradise and later descended to earth, but was civilized in spirit and nature; a prophet should not be imagined as an angel without human needs.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Âdem bile cennette çiftiyle yaratılmış, sonradan dünyaya inmiş, rûhen ve fıtraten medenî idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam and humanity uniquely received divine teaching and honor; angels were ordered to prostrate to Adam, and angels serve humans while humans are never tasked with serving angels.
rows.anchor: İmtihân-ı ilâhî ile Âdem melâikeye değil, melâike Âdem’e secde ile emrolunmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human status is the first condition of prophethood, whose distinguishing feature is special divine instruction through revelation; its duties of warning and good news carry heavy responsibilities.
rows.anchor: nübüvvetin ilk şartı insanlık, vasf-ı mümeyyizi de vahiy ile ta‘lîm-i mahsûs-ı ilâhîdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı argues that women's nature cannot bear prophetic duties; if God gave a woman that capacity, he says, it would transform her into a man, so the office belongs to the highest men.
rows.anchor: kadın fıtratı, dişi meşrebi doğrudan doğru bunun mes’ûliyetine mütehammil değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the thought that Bedouin detachment, resilience, or an unlettered recipient makes prophethood more fitting or revelation more miraculous for Bedouins.
rows.anchor: gibi de tevehhüm olunmamalıdır. Nübüvvet en büyük menba‘-ı medeniyet olduğu cihetle bedeviyet, nübüvvetin hikmet ve gayesiyle gayr-i mütenâsibdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Civilized communities, in his generalization, have more collective moral excellence, learning, forbearance, and alertness, while Bedouins are more ignorant, harsh, and hard-hearted.
rows.anchor: bedevîlerde cehl ü cefâ ve kasvet gālibdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites 9:97 for Bedouins' ignorance of revealed limits and a hadith saying that desert life makes one rough and hunting makes one heedless.
rows.anchor: وَأَجْدَرُ أَلَّا يَعْلَمُوا۟ حُدُودَ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ’dır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets have always come from civilized towns; Muhammad was sent from Mecca, the Mother of Towns, so rejection of him comes from shirk and dislike of truth rather than a scholarly reason.
rows.anchor: Hâtemü’l-enbiyâ da “Ümmü’l-kurâ” olan Mekke şehrinde doğup ba‘s buyurulmuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers are urged to travel and see how earlier peoples who claimed the world and associated partners with God met their end.
rows.anchor: baksalar a kendilerinden evvelkilerin âkıbetleri nasıl oldu?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife home is better for those who are God-conscious, and people are urged to use their reason to understand this.
rows.anchor: Ve her hâlde ittikā etmiş olanlar için âhiret evi daha hayırlı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When messengers despair of being heeded and disbelievers think the warning false, they mockingly ask when the promised judgment will come, as in 10:48.
rows.anchor: مَتَىٰ هَٰذَا ٱلْوَعْدُ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's aid then saves the messengers and those believers He wills, while the criminal peoples are destroyed; once God's judgment arrives, no force can avert it and repentance at despair is useless.
rows.anchor: Mevki‘-i icrâya konulmuş olan hükm-i Hak bozulmaz. Ve bu her zaman böyledir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stories of earlier prophets and peoples, especially Joseph and his brothers, teach those of sound intellect whose hearts are not corrupted by unhealthy feelings.
rows.anchor: evvelki enbiyâ ile ümmetlerinin ve bilhassa Yûsuf ve kardeşlerinin kıssasında

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an and this story are not fabricated; they confirm earlier revealed books, clarify all things, and guide and show mercy to believers who can benefit.
rows.anchor: bu -Kur’an, yahut bu güzel kıssa- Allah’ın mâdûnundan uydurulur bir söz değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who do not benefit from guidance await thunder and lightning; Elmalılı notes that Surah al-Ra'd follows this surah.
rows.anchor: Mâ‘adâsına gelince onlar bu hidâyet ve rahmetten intifâ‘etmezler. Göklerin gürlemesini, başlarına yıldırımların düşmesini

rows.speaker: Sâhib-i Keşşâf
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf treats subhan as a term for glorification, like the name Uthman, accusative through an omitted verb meaning I glorify God; it emphatically clears God of the faults enemies allege.
rows.anchor: Sâhib-i Keşşâf der ki “سُبْحَٰنَ tesbîhe alemdir

rows.speaker: Sâhib-i Keşşâf
rows.claim: In Surah al-Nur, al-Kashshaf says subhan was first used to glorify God upon seeing wondrous divine works and later extended to any wonder.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i Nûr’da da demiştir ki: “Bunda asıl, acâib[^3]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı rejects the idea that wonder cancels glorification: wonder is the occasion for tasbih, not a replacement for it.
rows.anchor: Bazıları bu surette tesbih mânasının sâkıt olacağını zannetmişlerse de doğru değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some restrict subhan's status as a proper name to its unannexed use; al-Baydawi simply calls it a name for glorification.
rows.anchor: Kâdî Beyzâvî اسم للتسبيح demekle iktifâ etmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir says subhan is a noun placed in the position of a verbal noun and made accusative because it occupies that position.
rows.anchor: İbn Cerîr de اسم وُضع موضع المصدر فنصب لوقوعه موقعه demiştir

rows.speaker: sâhib-i Kāmûs
rows.claim: The Qamus author says tasbih means God's sanctification, derives from sabaha, first meant hastening in worship, then generalized to spoken and enacted worship; subhana is a masdar like ghufran and later a name for tasbih.
rows.anchor: Kāmûs sahibi Besâir’de der ki: “‘Tesbih’ Allah’ı takdis demek olup ‘sebaha’dan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many reject the Qamus author's masdar analysis because the triliteral verb tasbih is unattested, calling subhan a noun placed in the masdar's position.
rows.anchor: çokları bunun masdar olduğunu kabul etmeyerek sâhib-i Kāmûs’u tahtı’e etmişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı asks which masdar subhan replaces: tasbih itself is a form-II masdar like tanzih and taqdis, so the better gloss here is God's self-transcendence, not merely declaring Him transcendent.
rows.anchor: burada سُبْحَٰنَ’yi “tenzih” ile değil, تنزّه االله بذاته وتعالى diye “tenezzüh” ile tefsir daha[^9] mânalıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this account subhan is a noun conveying God's essential purity and holiness, which Elmalılı suggests could be termed subhaniyet or sububiyet.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ’nın nezâhet ve kudsiyyet-i zâtiyesini ifade eder. Biz buna “sübhâniyet” veya “sübbûhiyet” diyebiliriz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A passive-result reading of tasbih approaches this sense but does not explicitly state God's essential purity, so it is not identical.
rows.anchor: nezâhet-i zâtiyede nas olmayacağı için aynı değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Subhan comes from subhana Allah and is most naturally annexed to Allah as its agent; the suppressed verb depends on context, and 30:17 gives the imperative sense glorify God.
rows.anchor: Ve سبحان’ın fâiline muzaf olması daha[^11] zâhirdir. Mukadder fiili de makamına göre takdir olunur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophetic report uses subuhat of God's face; some explain it as the face's light or beauty, others as divine majesty, while Elmalılı prefers manifestations of God's subhaniyya.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Peygamber’den rivayet olunan bir haberde لأََحْرَقَتْ سُبُحَاتُ وَجْهِهِ vârid olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second hadith says God's veil is light or fire and the splendors of His face would burn whatever His sight reaches; 7:143 provides a parallel in the mountain's crumbling.
rows.anchor: hicâbı nûr veya nârdır, onu açsa sübühât-ı vechi gözü ilişen her şeyi yakıverirdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah opens with exaltation because the miraculous Isra that follows needs acceptance and purification of hearts, and because God's power and generosity rule out incapacity or falsehood.
rows.anchor: isrâ hârikasını tebcil ve onu tasdik için kulûbun tasfiyesini temhid

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening also warns against imagining likenesses for God, relates to the coming destruction of al-Aqsa, and signals the surah's wider concern with divine transcendence.
rows.anchor: Mescid-i Aksâ’nın tahrîbi hâdisesi dolayısıyla da bu tenzîhin bir ehemmiyet-i mahsûsası vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's servant is Muhammad, His distinguished servant through worship; the Isra took a brief portion of one night.
rows.anchor: abdini O’na ibadetle mümtaz olan mâlum has kulunu, yani Muhammed Mustafa sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem’i

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Masjid al-Haram is the Kaaba and its sacred precinct, and the destination Masjid al-Aqsa is Bayt al-Maqdis in Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: Mescid-i Aksâ’ya -ki Beytü’l-Makdis’tir- İsrâ etti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The area around al-Aqsa was blessed with religious and worldly abundance: revelation and prophetic worship from Moses to Jesus, as well as rivers, trees, flowers, and fruits; Isra added further honor.
rows.anchor: Mûsâ aleyhisselâm’dan Îsâ aleyhisselâm’a kadar vahiy mehbiti, enbiyâ ibadetgâhı olmuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Isra hadith confirms that the Prophet rode Buraq to Bayt al-Maqdis; Ali al-Qari also cites a report blessing the land between al-Arish and the Euphrates, especially Palestine.
rows.anchor: İsrâ hadîsinde de “Burak’a bindim Beytü’l-Makdis’e vardım”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from third-person reference to first-person plural in barakna is an iltifat that introduces the wisdom of the Isra.
rows.anchor: âyetin bu noktasında gıyabdan tekellüme iltifat vâki‘olmuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Showing the Prophet God's signs means displaying immense wonders and taking him on the Mi'raj, as 53:18 says he saw his Lord's greatest signs.
rows.anchor: İsrâ ettik ki ona[^21] âyetlerimizden gösterelim için yani

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sound narrations in Bukhari and others say Muhammad rode Buraq to Bayt al-Maqdis, ascended through the heavens, met prophets, saw angels, Paradise and Hell, passed Sidrat al-Muntaha, and returned that night with the five prayers prescribed.
rows.anchor: Buhârî ve sâirede rivâyât-ı sahîha ile rivayet olunduğu üzere Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm Burak ile Beytü’l-Makdis’e vardıktan sonra

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Muhammad told Quraysh the next morning, some clapped in disbelief and some recent Muslims apostatized; Abu Bakr affirmed him because he already trusted the reports of heaven and prophethood, earning the title al-Siddiq.
rows.anchor: birtakım ricâl Ebû Bekir’e koştular “eğer o bunu söylediyse şüphesiz doğrudur” dedi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Questioned about Jerusalem, the Prophet was shown Bayt al-Maqdis and accurately described it to people who knew its features.
rows.anchor: derhâl Resûlullah’a Beytü’l-Makdis tecellî ettirildi, binâen‘aleyh ona bakıp tavsif ediyordu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet described a caravan at Rawha, a lost camel, and a water cup from which he drank and returned; he also recited the caravan's details and arrival time.
rows.anchor: Revha’da idi. Bir deve yitirmişler arıyorlardı, yüklerinde bir su kadehi vardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caravan arrived with the specified mottled white camel at sunrise, confirming the prophecy, but the Quraysh still called the sign clear magic, as 27:13 records.
rows.anchor: işte kervan geliyor, önünde bir cemel-i evrak ve[^27] içlerinde falan ve filan da var

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı rejects the view that the entire ascent used Buraq: Buraq carried the Prophet only to al-Aqsa, after which the Mi'raj was brought.
rows.anchor: tahkīki Mescid-i Aksâ’ya kadar İsrâ Burak ile olmuş, ba‘dehû Mi‘râc (asansör) kurulmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri reports that after leaving Bayt al-Maqdis the Mi'raj was brought; it was beautiful and carried the Prophet to the Gate of the Keepers.
rows.anchor: Ebû Sa‘îd-i Hudrî’den (radıyallâhu anh) rivayet olunduğu üzere Resûlullah buyurmuştur ki “Beytü’l-Makdis’te olandan fâriğ olduğumda Mi‘râc getirildi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Gate of the Keepers is the entrance to the lowest heaven, where its guardians wait, and 15:17 says the heavens are protected from every accursed devil.
rows.anchor: Hafaza kapısı semâ muhafızlarının beklediği semâ-yı dünya kapısıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri's second narration says Adam's descendants' souls ascend by the Mi'raj; at the lowest heaven, angel Ismail commands seventy thousand angels, each with a hundred thousand attendants, beyond whose number only God knows, as 74:31 says.
rows.anchor: Sonra Mi‘râc getirildi -ki Benî Âdem’in ervâhı onda urûc eder- baktım ki gördüğüm şeylerin en güzeli

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report says Adam, unchanged since creation, sees the souls of his descendants assigned to Illiyyin for believers and Sijjin for unbelievers; he welcomes Muhammad as a righteous prophet and son.
rows.anchor: mü’min rûhu ise ‘hoş rûh, hoş râyiha

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vision shows unjust consumers of orphans' property punished with cut lips and fire stones placed in their mouths and expelled below.
rows.anchor: dudaklarını kesiyorlar ve ağızlarına ateşten bir taş koyuyorlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Backbiters and slanderers who attack people's honor are made to eat strips cut from their skin, which they find repulsive.
rows.anchor: bunlar o hemmazlar, gammazlar ki nâsın etlerini yerler ve sebb ile ırz ve namuslarına taarruz ederler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adulterers leave fine roasted meat for carrion, representing their choice to abandon what God made lawful for what He forbade.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın helâl kıldığını bırakırlar da haram kıldığını yerler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Usurers with swollen bellies are trampled while Pharaoh's people are brought to the fire morning and evening; the vision alludes to the Qur'anic image in 2:275.
rows.anchor: Bunlar karınlarında ribâ yiyenler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Women suspended by their breasts or feet are identified as women who committed adultery and killed their children.
rows.anchor: zina eden ve evlatlarını öldüren kadınlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the second heaven Muhammad meets Joseph, whose face shines like the full moon, with followers from his community around him.
rows.anchor: ikinci semâya çıktık, orada Yûsuf ile buluştum, ümmetinden kendisine tâbi‘olanlar da etrafında idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the third heaven he meets the cousins John and Jesus, who look alike in clothing and hair.
rows.anchor: Yahyâ ve Îsâ ile buluştum

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the fourth heaven he meets Idris, whom God raised to a lofty place, as 19:57 states.
rows.anchor: İdris ile buluştum, bana selâm verdi, merhaba etti nitekim Allah teâlâ وَرَفَعْنَٰهُ مَكَانًا عَلِيًّا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the fifth heaven Aaron is surrounded by many followers and is described as beloved by his people with a very long beard.
rows.anchor: Orada kavmine sevdirilmiş olan Hârun ile buluştum. Etrafında ümmetinden birçok tebaası vardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the sixth heaven Moses says people presume he is God's most honored creation, yet Muhammad is more honored; he adds that prophets are accompanied by their followers.
rows.anchor: Nâs beni أَكْرَمُ الْخَلْقِ عَلَى االله zu‘m eder, bu ise Allah’a benden ekrem

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the seventh heaven Abraham leans on the Frequented House, welcomes Muhammad as righteous prophet and son, and identifies the Prophet's and his community's station; Muhammad recites 3:68 about Abraham's true followers.
rows.anchor: İbrâhim ile buluştum, sırtını Beyt-i Ma‘mûr’a dayamış, beni selâmladı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad prays in the Frequented House, which seventy thousand angels enter daily and never revisit.
rows.anchor: ona her gün yetmiş bin melek girer, kıyamete kadar avdet de etmezler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A tree has a spring branching into the River of Mercy and the Kawthar granted to Muhammad; he bathes in Mercy, is forgiven past and future sins, and enters a Paradise containing unimaginable delights.
rows.anchor: şu rahmet nehri, şu da Allah’ın sana verdiği Kevser

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God first prescribes fifty prayers; after Moses repeatedly advises Muhammad that his community cannot bear them, the number is reduced to five, which count as fifty.
rows.anchor: Sonunda beş namaz farz kıldı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report says good deeds count tenfold, an intended but unperformed good deed earns one, and an intended evil not done earns nothing while one committed is recorded once.
rows.anchor: hasene on misliyledir. Her kim haseneye himmet eder de onu işlemezse bir hasene yazıldı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı notes multiple Mi'raj reports in the canonical collections and says this report's chains appear in Ibn Jarir; its explicit account reaches the lowest heaven, while the rest is uncertain.
rows.anchor: bunda semâ-yı dünyaya kadar urûcun Mi‘râc ile olduğu musarrah, daha ilerisinde ise muhtemildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Citing Alusi from the Alai commentary, Elmalılı reports five mounts: Buraq to Jerusalem, Mi'raj to the first heaven, angel wings to the seventh, Gabriel's wing to Sidra, and Refref to the Throne's vicinity.
rows.anchor: Fakat Alâ’î[^41] Tefsiri’nden[^42] Âlûsî’nin nakline göre Resûlullah’ın İsrâ gecesi biniti beş idi
